en: Udāna 3.2 Nanda Sutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Nanda—the Blessed One’s brother, the son of his maternal aunt—announced this to a number of bhikkhus:
“Friends, I am practicing the holy life without delight.”
“I am unable to maintain the holy life; having renounced the training, I shall return to the lower life.
Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Sitting there, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, the Venerable Nanda—the Blessed One’s brother, the son of his maternal aunt—is reporting this to many bhikkhus:”
“‘Friends, I am dissatisfied with this holy life; I am unable to persevere in the holy life. Having renounced the training, I shall return to the lower life.
Then the Blessed One addressed a certain bhikkhu:
“Come, bhikkhu, address the bhikkhu Nanda in my name:”
“Friend Nanda, the Teacher summons you.
“Very well, Bhante,” that bhikkhu replied to the Blessed One, and he approached the Venerable Nanda. Having approached him, he said to the Venerable Nanda:
“Friend Nanda, the Teacher summons you.”
“Yes, friend,” the Venerable Nanda replied to that bhikkhu.
He then approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As the Venerable Nanda was sitting there, the Blessed One said this to him:
“Is it true, Nanda, that you reported this to many bhikkhus:
‘Friends, I am dissatisfied with the holy life; I am unable to endure the holy life. Having renounced the training, I shall return to the lower life’?
“It is true, Bhante.”
“But why, Nanda, do you live the holy life dissatisfied, unable to endure the holy life, so that you will renounce the training and return to the low life?
“Venerable sir, when I was leaving my home, the Sakyan lady Janapadakalyāṇī looked at me with her hair only half-shaved and said this to me:
‘May you return quickly, noble son.’”
“Thus, venerable sir, recollecting that [past], I am dissatisfied with the holy life; I am unable to maintain the holy life. Having renounced the training, I shall return to the lower life.

Then the Blessed One took the Venerable Nanda by the arm—just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm—so too, having vanished from Jeta’s Grove, he appeared in the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
He appeared among the Tāvatiṃsa gods.
Now at that time, about five hundred nymphs with feet like those of a cock had come into the presence of Sakka, lord of the devas.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Nanda:
“Nanda, do you see these five hundred nymphs with feet like those of a rooster? “I do, Bhante.
“What do you think, Nanda: which is more beautiful, more lovely, or more charming—the most beautiful woman in the land of the Sakyans, or these five hundred nymphs with feet like those of a rooster?”
“Venerable sir, just as a female monkey with its ears and nose cut off would be,

even so, venerable sir, that Sākiyan lady, the most beautiful woman in the land, does not even approach these five hundred celestial nymphs by way of number, nor does she approach them by way of fraction,
nor does she approach them by way of comparison. Rather, these five hundred celestial nymphs are more beautiful, more lovely to behold, and more pleasing.”
“Delight, Nanda! Delight, Nanda!
I am your guarantor for the acquisition of five hundred kakuṭapāda nymphs.
“If, venerable sir, the Blessed One is my guarantor for the acquisition of five hundred kakuṭapāda nymphs, I will delight, venerable sir, in the holy life under the Blessed One.”
Then the Blessed One took the Venerable Nanda by the arm—
just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm— so too, vanishing from among the Tāvatiṃsa devas,
he reappeared at Jeta’s Grove.
The bhikkhus heard:
"It is said that the Venerable Nanda, the Blessed One’s brother and son of his maternal aunt, is living the holy life for the sake of celestial nymphs;
it is said that the Blessed One has guaranteed him the acquisition of five hundred kakuṭapāda nymphs."
Then the venerable Nanda’s fellow monks addressed the venerable Nanda with the term "hireling" and the term "bargain-purchase," saying: "The venerable Nanda is indeed a hireling;
the venerable Nanda is indeed a bargain-purchase. He lives the holy life for the sake of celestial nymphs;
it is said that the Blessed One has guaranteed him the acquisition of five hundred kakuṭapāda nymphs."
Then the Venerable Nanda, distressed, ashamed, and disgusted by his fellow monks’ talk of him as a hireling and a servant,
dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute,
in no long time attained that supreme goal of the holy life for the sake of which sons of good family rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.
Having realized it for himself through direct higher knowledge in this very life, he entered and dwelt therein.
He directly knew: "Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.
And so, the Venerable Nanda became one of the Arahants.
Then, when the night was far spent, a certain deity of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One.
Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, she stood to one side.
Standing to one side, that deity said this to the Blessed One:

“Venerable sir, the Venerable Nanda, the Blessed One’s brother and son of his maternal aunt, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom through the destruction of the taints, dwells having attained it.
Then the knowledge arose in the Blessed One as well:

“Nanda, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom through the destruction of the taints, dwells having attained it.”
Then, when that night had passed, the Venerable Nanda approached the Blessed One;
having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Nanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, regarding that promise which the Blessed One made for me to obtain five hundred kakuṭapāda nymphs—I release the Blessed One from that commitment.”
“Nanda, I too have encompassed your mind with my own mind and known:

‘Nanda, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having entered upon it and remained therein.
Deities also have reported this matter to me:”

“Venerable sir, the Venerable Nanda, the Blessed One’s brother and the son of his maternal aunt, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom through the destruction of the taints, dwells having attained it.
“Nanda, as soon as your mind was liberated from the taints through non-clinging, at that moment I myself was released from that promise.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“He for whom the mire has been crossed over,
who has crushed the thorn of sensual desire,
and who has reached the destruction of delusion— ”
“He does not waver in the face of pleasure and pain—he is a bhikkhu. Thus ends the second [sutta].
